prompt: The dashed line shows the path of a hockey ball scooped into the air, moving from A to D. At which of the labelled positions is the ball's acceleration directed vertically downward?
options: At all four positions A, B, C and D
At D only
At C and D only
At B, C and D only
answer: At all four positions A, B, C and D
hint: Once the ball leaves the stick, the only force on it is gravity, which acts straight down at every point of the flight.

prompt: The strobe diagram shows a black ball dropped from rest and a white ball projected horizontally, released at the same instant. The diagram shows that at each flash the two balls are at the same height and have fallen the same distance.
options: True
False
hint: Horizontal and vertical motion are independent; the horizontal launch of the white ball does not change how it falls.

prompt: For the frictionless banked curve shown, calculate the maximum safe speed in m s$^{-1}$. Take $g = 9.8$ m s$^{-2}$.
hint: Read the radius (63 m) and banking angle (12 degrees) from the diagram, then use $v = \sqrt{rg\tan\theta}$.

prompt: For the current-carrying loop WXYZ in the magnetic field shown (field lines up the page, current direction marked), what are the directions of the forces on sides WZ and XY?
options: Force on WZ is into the page; force on XY is out of the page
Force on WZ is out of the page; force on XY is into the page
Both forces are into the page
Both forces are out of the page
answer: Force on WZ is into the page; force on XY is out of the page
hint: Apply $F = I\vec{L} \times \vec{B}$ to each side; the currents in WZ and XY run in opposite directions, so the forces are opposite, giving a torque.

prompt: The two diagrams contain the same number of magnetic field lines, but the left-hand region is smaller. Which statement is correct?
options: Both show the same magnetic flux, and the smaller region has the greater flux density
Both show the same flux and the same flux density
The smaller region shows less flux and a lower flux density
The smaller region shows more flux and a lower flux density
answer: Both show the same magnetic flux, and the smaller region has the greater flux density
hint: Flux is the total number of field lines; flux density is that number divided by the area they pass through.

prompt: Using the spanner length, force and angle shown in the diagram, calculate the magnitude of the torque applied to the nut.
Using the currents and separations shown for the three parallel rods, calculate the magnitude of the net force per unit length on rod C. Use $\mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7}$ N A$^{-2}$.
hint: Rod B carries current the same way as C (attraction, 0.20 m away); rod A carries it the opposite way (repulsion, 0.30 m away). Work out $\dfrac{\mu_0 I_1 I_2}{2\pi r}$ for each and combine.

prompt: In which direction does the net force per unit length on rod C act?
options: Towards rod B (up the page)
Towards rod A (down the page)
Along the length of rod C
There is no net force on rod C
hint: Rod B attracts C (same current direction) and is closer than rod A, which repels C, so B's pull wins.

prompt: The conducting rod slides to the right along the rails, through a magnetic field directed into the page. Which row is correct?
options: Force on the rod: to the left. Induced current in the rod: upward. Current around the loop: anticlockwise
Force to the left; current downward in the rod; clockwise around the loop
Force to the right; current upward in the rod; anticlockwise around the loop
Force to the right; current downward in the rod; clockwise around the loop
answer: Force on the rod: to the left. Induced current in the rod: upward. Current around the loop: anticlockwise
hint: The area of the loop, and so the flux into the page, is increasing; the induced current opposes that increase, and the force opposes the rod's motion.

prompt: In the apparatus shown, the rubber stopper is swung in a horizontal circle on a string that runs through the tube to a hanging mass. The swing rate is adjusted until the hanging mass neither rises nor falls, then the radius is measured. Match each quantity to its role in the investigation.

pairs.item: Rate of rotation of the stopper

hint: The quantity deliberately changed is independent; the one then measured is dependent; anything held fixed is controlled.

prompt: In the double-slit set-up shown, the distance between the slits and the screen is increased while everything else stays the same. What happens to the spacing between the bright bands?
options: It increases
It decreases
It stays the same
The bright bands disappear
hint: Fringe spacing $\Delta y = \dfrac{\lambda L}{d}$ is directly proportional to the slit-to-screen distance $L$.

prompt: If instead the separation between the two slits were increased (with the screen distance unchanged), the spacing between the bright bands would decrease.
options: True
False
hint: $\Delta y = \dfrac{\lambda L}{d}$ is inversely proportional to the slit separation $d$.

prompt: Unpolarised light of intensity 150 W m$^{-2}$ passes through polariser P1 (axis 30 degrees to the vertical) and then P2 (axis horizontal), as shown. Calculate the intensity transmitted through P2.
hint: P1 halves the intensity to 75 W m$^{-2}$; the angle between P1 and P2 is 60 degrees, so $I = 75\cos^2 60^\circ$.

prompt: Using the mercury energy-level diagram, calculate the frequency of the photon emitted when an electron falls from the n = 5 level to the n = 3 level. Use $h = 6.626 \times 10^{-34}$ J s and $1$ eV $= 1.602 \times 10^{-19}$ J.
hint: Read the two level energies from the diagram ($-3.71$ eV and $-5.52$ eV); the photon energy is their difference, 1.81 eV, then $f = E/h$.

prompt: Model 1 and Model 2 show alpha particles passing through two models of the atom. Which option correctly identifies the models?
options: Model 1 is Thomson's model (alpha particles barely deflected by the spread-out charge); Model 2 is Rutherford's model (a few alpha particles deflected sharply by a tiny dense nucleus)
Model 1 is Rutherford's model; Model 2 is Thomson's model
Both diagrams show Rutherford's nuclear model
Both diagrams show Thomson's plum-pudding model
answer: Model 1 is Thomson's model (alpha particles barely deflected by the spread-out charge); Model 2 is Rutherford's model (a few alpha particles deflected sharply by a tiny dense nucleus)
hint: Only a small, dense, concentrated positive charge can push an alpha particle through a large angle.
